problems.title: Orthogonal projection does not preserve an objective after a positive finite step
problems.source_location: Theorem 3.1, PDF p. 5; Theorem B.2, PDF p. 14.
claim: Paraphrase: Theorem 3.1, p. 5, and its restatement as Theorem B.2, p. 14, assert that differentiable \(L\)-smooth individual and collective objectives both do not decrease under the FCGrad update for sufficiently small \(\eta>0\). The conflict-case proof uses \(b^\top g=0\) to infer preservation of the collective objective.
analysis: At \((0,0)\), take bounded \(1\)-smooth objectives \(I(x,y)=\sin x+\sin y\) and \(C(x,y)=1-\sin x+\cos y\). Their gradients are \((1,1)\) and \((-1,0)\); conflict projection leaves direction \((0,1)\), orthogonal to \(\nabla C\). Nevertheless \(C(0,\eta)=1+\cos\eta<2=C(0,0)\) for every sufficiently small \(\eta>0\). A zero directional derivative does not ensure a nonnegative finite-step change.
result: The theorem's finite-step protection is false under its smoothness assumptions. The example leaves observed empirical gains unadjudicated.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
repair: The existing direction supports first-order protection only: smoothness gives \(C(\theta+\eta g)-C(\theta)\geq-L\eta^2\|g\|^2/2\). A separate proposed common-ascent modification applies only to noncollinear conflicting gradients: for \(q=a^\top b<0\), let \(h=a-qb/\|b\|^2\), \(m=\|h\|^2>0\), and \(d=h+mb/[2(-q)]\). Then \(a^\top d=m/2>0\), \(b^\top d>0\); a sufficiently small step improves both fixed-agent objectives. This changes the algorithm and does not establish fairness convergence or simultaneous-agent improvement.
problems.impact_rationale: The bounded smooth counterexample violates the main finite-step nondecrease guarantee for every sufficiently small positive step. This directly falsifies a central theorem and warrants Major.

problems.title: Recurrent conflicts can leave a nonzero value gap forever
problems.source_location: Theorem 3.2, PDF p. 5; Theorem B.5, PDF p. 16.
claim: Paraphrase: Theorem 3.2, p. 5, and Theorem B.5, p. 16, assume \(L\)-smooth values, \(\delta_t=V_{\rm ind}(\theta_t)-V_{\rm col}(\theta_t)\), positive steps satisfying
analysis: Let \(I(\theta)=\sin\theta\), \(C(\theta)=1-\sin\theta\), and \(\theta_0=0\). Their opposing gradients \(1,-1\) project to zero, so every iterate remains zero and the value gap stays \(-1\). Steps \(\eta_t=1/(t+1)\) satisfy the upper bound, divergent sum and square-summable condition with \(L=1\). Conflict recurs forever without progress toward equal values.
result: The universal fairness-convergence conclusion requires a nondegeneracy or progress assumption absent from the stated theorem.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
problems.impact_rationale: An admissible recurrent-conflict trajectory satisfies the step conditions but keeps a nonzero value gap forever. This falsifies the main fairness-convergence guarantee and warrants Major.

problems.title: Local guarantees do not imply individual improvement under simultaneous multi-agent updates
problems.source_location: Paragraph following Theorem 3.1 and Section 3.1 single-agent parameters, PDF p. 5.
claim: The paragraph immediately after Theorem 3.1, p. 5, extends the single-agent result to all agents when all use FCGrad. The mathematical objects in Section 3.1 are gradients with respect to the parameters of one agent.
analysis: Take returns \(R_1=\sin\theta_1-3\sin\theta_2\) and \(R_2=3\sin\theta_1+4\sin\theta_2\), with collective return \((R_1+R_2)/2\). At zero, with the allowed mixing weight \(\beta=1/2\), the nonconflict FCGrad directions are \(1.5\) and \(2.25\). Each own-coordinate update improves its local objectives, but their simultaneous effect on \(R_1\) has derivative \(1.5-3(2.25)=-5.25\). The single-agent argument leaves these cross-agent terms uncontrolled.
result: The stated simultaneous-update extension does not follow and fails on this bounded smooth game. A separate multi-agent guarantee would need additional assumptions.
assumptions: The finding is restricted to the identified paper version and identified released component; published experiment provenance is not inferred from public code alone.
problems.impact_rationale: Cross-agent derivatives make an individual's return fall under the asserted simultaneous-update extension. This directly contradicts the stated multi-agent guarantee and warrants Major.
